chose subscription ($7/mo) over one-time purchase, betting on recurring productivity use, not novelty

earned press (Engadget, Cybernews CES coverage) as the acquisition channel instead of paid ads

case_name: Meta Quest / Horizon Store solo & lean-studio developers
product: VR titles on Meta Horizon Store / App Lab, various genres
revenue_range: platform paid ~$20M via Horizon+ subscription payouts across all participating devs in 2025; individual solo dev figures undisclosed
failure_modes_survived: $20-40 average title price (far above mobile norms) shows VR/spatial buyers tolerate premium pricing
Meta explicitly built monetization/discovery tooling usable by solo devs with no marketing staff
honest_flaw: Requires a Quest headset build, not a webcam/browser app — a platform and packaging shift operator has not made. Aggregate $20M payout is across many developers, not evidence any single solo dev is thriving; 30% platform commission also applies.

case_name: Apple Vision Pro indie developer economics (general)
revenue_range: ~$25,000 gross best-case cited for a $9.99 app at 5% discovery / 10% conversion, before Apple's cut
honest_flaw: This is presented as a WARNING case, not a success: installed base still under 500K units, six months of dev time can net less than one developer's half-year salary. Cited here because it directly tells operator NOT to bet on the native visionOS App Store as the near-term path; enterprise seat licensing ($50-100/seat) is flagged as the only economically sane VR path, and that requires B2B sales cycles operator hasn't built yet.

case_name: Pieter Levels (NomadList / RemoteOK / PhotoAI) — build-in-public reference pattern
product: Portfolio of small web tools (not spatial), built and marketed entirely in public
failure_modes_survived: ships fast, ugly, public — revenue screenshots ARE the marketing channel
never waited for a polished product before charging money
honest_flaw: Not spatial/gesture/AR at all — pure web SaaS. Included only because it is THE most-cited solo-dev build-in-public case in 2026 search results, and operator explicitly asked how to go from 'building privately' to 'building publicly.' The transferable lesson is the public-building mechanic, not the product category.
